products.superPrompt:
You are a puzzle constructor and a stationery designer. Your goal: produce the complete content of a 40-page printable "Analog Bag Refill Pack": pocket booklets a buyer prints, folds and tucks into a tote or stocking as a screen-free gift.

BUYER AND JOB: Gen Z and millennial women aged 18-34 who carry an "analog bag" (a tote of screen-free activities) so they reach for it instead of their phone, plus friends and parents buying them a last-minute, low-cost gift. Most screen-free printables are kids' coloring packs; this one is written for adults and teens, fully original, and gift-ready.

USE YOUR CODE TOOL (Python) to build and verify every puzzle. If you have no code tool, say so at the top and make only small puzzles you can check by listing each answer's grid coordinates.

DELIVERABLE: pages are half-letter 5.5x8.5 in (I will also make A5 148x210 mm), 0.4 in margins, printed as fold-in-half booklets.
Booklet 1 "Pocket Puzzles" (16 pages): cover; how to play; 4 criss-cross crosswords (12-14 words each; themes: cozy evenings, things in a tote, winter walks, paper and ink) with original clues; 4 word searches (13x13 grid, 14 words, uppercase; words run forward, down or diagonally down only; themes: library, crafts, tea time, winter); 3 logic-grid puzzles (3 categories x 4 items, 5-7 clues, a two-line story, exactly one solution); 3 pages of answer keys.
Booklet 2 "Sketch Something" (8 pages): cover plus 30 sketch prompts, 4-5 per page, each with an empty frame.
Booklet 3 "52 Weeks of Pages" (8 pages): cover, 52 journal prompts numbered by week, and a notes page.
Loose pages: "Offline Bingo" (5x5 card: 24 phone-free activities and a free center square "Phone in another room"); a "What's in my analog bag" checklist; a one-sheet 8-panel mini-zine "A Pocket Guide to Going Analog" (US Letter landscape; say which panels print upside down and give fold-and-cut steps); a gift-tag page (4 tags at 2.5x4 in reading "Your analog bag awaits" with To and From lines); a printing-and-folding instructions page.

DESIGN: Palette "Oat & Ink": Oat Paper #F4EDE1, Graphite #2E2E2E, Tomato #D9583B, Moss #6B7B4B, Denim #3E5C76, Butter #F2C94C. Fonts: Playfair Display (titles), Courier Prime (grid numbers, labels), Lato (body, 10 pt minimum), Caveat (handwritten accents). Keep it ink-light: white page backgrounds with small color accents. Give layout notes for every page: title area, grid size in inches, frame positions.

PUZZLE ACCURACY (must pass):
- Crosswords: show each grid as rows of characters with # for empty cells, the numbering, Across and Down clues and answers; confirm every crossing letter matches and every listed word appears exactly once.
- Word searches: print 13 rows of 13 letters; give each word's start cell and direction; confirm with code that each word appears exactly once; fill the rest with random letters and regenerate if any rude or unintended word appears.
- Logic grids: brute-force all combinations to confirm exactly one solution; give the solution table.
- Write every clue, story and prompt from scratch; never copy published puzzles; no famous names, brands, films, songs or games in answers or clues.

PROMPTS: Sketch and journal prompts are concrete, playful and doable in 5-15 minutes; mix observation ("the view from your usual seat"), memory and imagination; nothing that needs a phone; inclusive and non-religious; reading level grade 6-8; no therapy language and no promises about mood, focus, health or productivity.

DIFFERENTIATION: Adult and teen voice, gift packaging (tag, booklet fold), all puzzles original and verified, and a coordinated look that matches a companion tote.

CONSTRAINTS: Use "analog" as a plain word only. No brand names (no puzzle, newspaper, camera, phone, app or social-media brands), no daily five-letter guessing grids or other branded game formats, no real people or creators.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Part 1: Booklet 1 page by page with complete puzzles and answer keys. Part 2: Booklets 2 and 3. Part 3: loose pages. Write each page as "PAGE n | title | layout | exact text or grid". If your tool can save files, also render each puzzle grid and answer key as a 300 DPI PNG on a transparent background. Stop after each part and wait for me to type "continue".

SELF-CHECK before each part: page counts 16/8/8; 30 sketch prompts; 52 journal prompts; 24 bingo squares plus the free center; every puzzle verified as above and every answer key matching its puzzle; no brand names, claims or copied text. Fix anything that fails, then answer.

asymmetry.badBetIf: The input found no direct proof that people pay for printable analog-bag content rather than physical fillers, and free sites already give away coloring pages. If page 1 of Etsy for 'analog bag' already shows adult puzzle packs under $5, or the puzzles cannot be verified (broken crosswords lead to bad reviews), do not build it.

risks: Puzzle quality: AI-made crosswords and word searches are often broken; verify with code and hand-check before listing.
Demand uncertainty: purchase intent is proven for physical screen-free gifts, not for printables.
Free competition (analogbag.net and others) could fill the adult segment.
Timing: new Etsy listings need weeks to surface, so an October listing is essential for the Nov-Dec gift peak.
Claims: avoid any mental-health or 'detox' benefit language in copy and pins.
Rights: never imitate branded puzzle formats or name camera, phone or club brands; check 'analog bag' for trademark filings before using it heavily in titles (not checked in the input).

products.superPrompt:
You are a party-game designer and a relaxed, generous holiday host. Your goal: produce the complete content of a printable "Phone-Free Table Kit" in two editions, Friendsgiving and Christmas/New Year's Eve, that a host downloads, prints at home and uses the same night.

BUYER AND JOB: Friendsgiving and holiday-dinner hosts aged 18-35. Their friends say time together matters more than presents, and phone-free events are growing; hosts want an easy, kind way to get phones off the table and keep conversation going, without lecturing anyone.

DELIVERABLE (each edition; US Letter 8.5x11 in, and I will make A4 copies, so keep a 0.25 in safe margin; ink-light white backgrounds with color accents):
1. Phone-basket sign, 5x7 in, 2 per landscape sheet: "Phones rest here tonight" plus an editable line such as "Back after dessert". Also a basket label, 4x2 in.
2. 60 conversation cards, 2.5x3.5 in, 9 per sheet (3x3), 7 sheets (the last 3 slots are blank "Write your own" cards) plus one card-back sheet for double-sided printing. Three decks of 20: Warm-Up (easy and funny), Story Time (memories and favorites), What If (imagination). 45 cards are shared by both editions and 15 are seasonal (5 per deck).
3. Four original pen-and-paper party games, each with a one-page rules card (half-letter 5.5x8.5 in) and a score or play sheet if needed: (a) a write-draw-write paper telephone game; (b) a timed letter-and-category listing game; (c) an anonymous "guess who wrote it" answers game; (d) a fold-over drawing game (head, body, legs). Give each an original name and complete rules: players, time, materials, setup, how to play, scoring, and variations for 4 players and for 12 or more.
4. Place cards: tents 3.5x2 in folded (3.5x4 in flat), 4 per sheet, editable name on the front and a "question for your neighbor" on the back.
5. Host note, 5x7 in: three short versions (playful, warm, a text message to send guests beforehand) that explain the phone basket in a friendly way.
6. Instructions page: printing, cutting, and a 3-step evening flow (arrival: basket; dinner: cards; dessert: games).

DESIGN: Friendsgiving "Harvest Table": Cream #FBF5EA, Pumpkin #D9772B, Cranberry #9E2B3A, Sage #8DA47E, Bark #4A3B2F. Winter/NYE "Candlelight": Snow #F8F8F5, Midnight #1E2A44, Gold #C9A44C, Evergreen #2F5D50, Berry #A23B4D. Fonts: DM Serif Display (headings), Nunito (body, 10 pt minimum), Caveat (accents). Give layout notes for each sheet: grid, card front and back layout, icon spots.

CONTENT RULES: Original wording; warm, playful, never preachy or anti-technology; reading level grade 6-8; gender-neutral; works for mixed ages 13+ and for guests who do not celebrate the holiday. Cards avoid politics, religion, money, bodies, dating status, trauma and heavy confessions; each can be answered by anyone in under 2 minutes. No claims about health, wellbeing, "detox" or relationship outcomes.

DIFFERENTIATION: Phone-free is the hook, which generic Friendsgiving trivia and invitations do not address; signage, cards, games and place cards form one coordinated system; place cards carry neighbor questions; two editions share one design system.

CONSTRAINTS: Do not use or allude to trademarked game names (for example Pictionary, Scattergories, Telestrations, Taboo, Codenames, Mad Libs, Heads Up) or their exact formats or card layouts; no phone or app brands; no named clubs, events or creators; no song lyrics, film or TV references; no real people.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Edition 1 (Friendsgiving), then Edition 2 (Winter/NYE), sheet by sheet as "SHEET n | piece | size and grid | layout | exact text". Write the 45 shared cards once, then each edition's 15 seasonal cards and seasonal sign and host-note lines. If you run out of space, stop after Edition 1 and wait for me to type "continue".

SELF-CHECK before answering: 60 cards per edition (45 shared + 15 seasonal), 20 per deck, no duplicates or near-duplicates, no banned topics; 4 games with complete, playable rules and original names; 9 cards fit a Letter sheet (7.5x10.5 in) and an A4 sheet (190.5x266.7 mm); no brand or trademarked game names; no claims. Fix anything that fails, then answer.

products.themeKey: An illustrated 'contents map' tote: line drawings of a paper
products.superPrompt:
You are an illustrator and print-on-demand designer. Your goal: produce the complete design package for an illustrated "contents map" tote bag, a canvas tote whose artwork shows what goes inside an analog bag, sold on Etsy through Printify.

BUYER AND JOB: Analog-curious Gen Z and millennials, and people buying a tote to build an analog bag as a gift. The bag is the object at the center of the trend, so this tote is both the gift and the container; it pairs with a printable "Analog Bag Refill Pack".

DELIVERABLE:
1. Phrase options: 12 original short phrases (2-4 words) for the top of the design in the spirit of "Gone analog", plain and warm, no puns on brands. Rank them and flag each "needs a USPTO trademark search before use"; never present any phrase as cleared.
2. Composition spec for a single-color line drawing on a 14x14 in square master (4200x4200 px at 300 DPI, transparent background), centered: a dashed outline of an open tote containing 6 items drawn in a loose, overlapping arrangement: a paperback with a blank cover, a boxy generic film camera (rangefinder-like rectangle, no instant-camera shape, no logo, no lens text), a ball of yarn with a crochet hook, a small folded pocket puzzle booklet, a pencil, and a small notebook. Each item gets a small number in a circle; a legend below reads like a map key (for example "1 a paperback 2 a camera 3 yarn & hook 4 a pocket puzzle 5 a pencil 6 a notebook"; write the final legend text). Give the item positions as a 3x3 grid layout and the phrase position.
3. Print rules: minimum line weight about 2 pt at final size; no fine hatching or tiny text under 14 pt; one ink color; text set later in a typed font, not drawn by the image AI. Ink versions: Graphite #2E2E2E on a natural tote, Denim #3E5C76 as an alternate, and Oat #F4EDE1 for a black tote.
4. Three image-generation prompts I can paste into an image model: (a) the main line drawing, (b) a looser hand-drawn alternate, (c) the six items as separate sticker-style icons for spin-offs. Each states the style, composition, colors with hex codes, aspect ratio 1:1, transparent or pure white background, and negatives (no text, no logos, no brand shapes, no people, no watermarks).
5. Typography: a font for the phrase (such as Playfair Display Italic or DM Serif Display) and for the legend (Caveat or Courier Prime), with sizes in points at the 14 in width.
6. A mockup shot list of 7 listing images (flat lay, packed with refill booklets, on a shoulder with no face, detail of the legend, size guide, gift-set image, color options) and a 3-line gift-set note that tells buyers how the refill pack pairs with the tote.

CONTENT RULES: Everything original; plain, friendly wording; reading level grade 6-8; no claims about health, focus or screen time.

DIFFERENTIATION: Illustration-led rather than slogan-only; the legend makes it a "map" of an analog bag; it coordinates with the Refill Pack's "Oat & Ink" palette (Oat #F4EDE1, Graphite #2E2E2E, Tomato #D9583B, Moss #6B7B4B, Denim #3E5C76, Butter #F2C94C).

CONSTRAINTS: No brands or trade dress: nothing resembling Polaroid, Instax or Fujifilm cameras, Brick or Light Phone devices, The Offline Club, or any newspaper puzzle or daily word-game branding; no book titles; no creators' names or likenesses; no song lyrics or film references.

OUTPUT FORMAT: Numbered sections 1-6 as above, written so I can work through them in order in Canva and Printify. End with a self-check: phrases flagged for a trademark search; the camera described as generic; line-weight and text-size rules stated; all three image prompts include negatives and a 1:1 aspect ratio; no brand names appear except in the "do not resemble" list. Fix anything that fails, then answer.

assembly: Run the super prompt in Claude or ChatGPT; pick 2-3 phrases and check each in the USPTO trademark search (tmsearch.uspto.gov) and on Etsy for existing use before choosing one (not done in the input). If anything looks close, use another phrase.

Generate the main artwork; reject any result whose camera looks like a real brand or model. If you only get a white background, remove it (Canva Pro background remover or a free remover) and upscale to at least 4200 x 4200 px with an upscaler; for the crispest lines, trace it to vector in Inkscape (free) before export.

In Canva create a 4200 x 4200 px design, place the art, add the numbers in the circles, the legend (Caveat or Courier Prime) and the chosen phrase (Playfair Display Italic or DM Serif Display), keep all text above about 14 pt at print size, then download as PNG with a transparent background. Make an Oat #F4EDE1 ink version for a black tote.

In Printify choose a natural cotton canvas tote with a US print provider (compare base cost, ratings and production time in the catalog), download or view its print-area template, and scale the PNG to fit inside the print area with the composition centered.

Generate Printify mockups (front, close-up, both colors), connect Printify to your Etsy shop, set the price ($28 with free shipping built in), and publish. Add the print provider as a production partner in Etsy as Etsy requires for print-on-demand items.

Order one sample to your own address on Day 0; when it arrives, check line sharpness and placement, then photograph it packed with printed refill booklets and replace the mockups as the first listing photos.
Upload the same art to Redbubble (tote bags and stickers) as a no-cost secondary listing.
products.listingPrompt:
You are an Etsy SEO copywriter. Write the Etsy listing for a print-on-demand canvas tote bag with an original illustrated "contents map" of an analog bag: line drawings of a paperback, a generic film camera, yarn and a crochet hook, a pocket puzzle booklet, a pencil and a notebook, each numbered with a map-style legend, and the phrase [YOUR CHOSEN PHRASE].
Product facts to fill from my Printify product page: tote model and size [SIZE], fabric [FABRIC], handle length [HANDLES], print method [PRINT METHOD], production time [DAYS], US shipping time [DAYS]; printed and shipped by my print partner [PROVIDER NAME]. Gift-set option: buyers can add the printable Analog Bag Refill Pack (separate digital listing) [LINK].

Produce:
1. TITLE under 140 characters starting with the buyer's search phrase (choose from "Analog Bag Tote", "Book Lover Tote Bag", "Canvas Tote Bag Gift"), then the design (illustrated contents map, paperback, camera, yarn) and gift use. Sentence case; show the character count.
2. 13 TAGS of 20 characters or fewer (show each count), no repeats, from phrases like: analog bag, analog bag tote, canvas tote bag, book lover tote, reader gift, crochet tote, gift for her, screen free gift, cute tote bag, illustrated tote, bookish gift, aesthetic tote, christmas gift tote.
3. DESCRIPTION: a 2-line opening; what the illustration shows; tote specifications from the facts above; care instructions (cold wash inside out or spot clean; check the provider's care guidance); production and shipping times with a clear "order by [DATE] for Christmas delivery" line that I will set from my provider's cutoffs; the gift-set note; a line that the design was created with AI assistance and finished by me, and that it is printed by a production partner; a 4-question FAQ (What size is it? Is the print one color? Can I get it on a black tote? When will it arrive?).
RULES: No trademarked or brand terms anywhere (no camera, phone, puzzle, newspaper or app brands, no named clubs or creators); do not call the camera by any brand or model. No claims about health, focus or screen time. Do not promise delivery dates the provider does not guarantee. Output in order: Title, Tags, Description.

pricing.rationale: At an estimated $13 base plus $6 US shipping, $28 with free shipping leaves about $6 after Etsy fees (estimate). Below $24 the margin nearly disappears, and above about $34 it competes with branded gift totes. Margins are thin, so the tote is mainly a gift-set anchor for the Refill Pack.

asymmetry.badBetIf: You treat it as a standalone money-maker: it is not very asymmetric on its own (thin margin, deadline, crowded). Skip it if the sample prints poorly on canvas, the chosen phrase has trademark conflicts, or you cannot list by Oct 15.

risks: Thin margins: provider price or shipping changes can erase the roughly $6 profit; recheck costs in the catalog before publishing.
Trademark: the phrase (including 'Gone analog') is unchecked; search before use.
Brand resemblance: AI cameras often look like real models; keep it generic or redraw it.
Print quality: thin lines can break up on canvas; follow the line-weight rule and confirm with the sample.
December delays: provider production and carrier delays can miss Christmas; state cutoffs clearly and avoid promising dates.
Policy: Etsy requires print-on-demand production partners to be disclosed in listings; AI-assisted design should be disclosed too (check current policies).
